title: Shopify Dev Handoff — Figma Frame to Shopify File Mapping
content:
For a clean developer handoff, every Figma frame must map 1:1 to a Shopify file. This is not optional — developers literally name their files after your Figma layer names.

FILE MAPPING HIERARCHY:
Figma Page → Shopify template type (e.g., 'product', 'collection', 'index', 'article', 'customers/account')
Figma Frame (page artboard) → Shopify JSON template file (e.g., templates/product.json)
Figma Section Frame (child of artboard) → Shopify section file (e.g., sections/product-information.liquid)
Figma Block Component → Shopify block file (e.g., blocks/product-image.liquid) or inline block schema
Figma Layout Component → Shopify layout/theme.liquid (shared across all templates)

NAMING CONVENTION:
Figma page: 'template-product' → Shopify: templates/product.json
Figma page: 'template-collection' → Shopify: templates/collection.json
Figma page: 'template-index' → Shopify: templates/index.json (home page)
Figma frame: 'section-hero' → Shopify: sections/hero.liquid
Figma frame: 'section-product-information' → Shopify: sections/product-information.liquid
Figma component: 'block-product-image' → Shopify block in schema: type: 'product-image'
Figma component: 'block-text' → Shopify: type: 'text'
Figma component: 'layout-default' → Shopify: layout/theme.liquid

PRAGMATIC NAMING RULES:
— Use kebab-case for all Figma frame/component names that map to Shopify files
— Never use spaces in section/block names — developers copy them directly
— Prefix sections with 'section-', blocks with 'block-' in Figma layer panel
— Always name the shared header/footer wrapper 'layout-default'
— For alternate templates (e.g., landing page product), name as 'template-product-landing'

FRAME STRUCTURE EXAMPLE:
  Page: 'template-product'
    Frame: 'layout-default' (shared — only needs designing once)
      Frame: 'section-header'
      Frame: 'section-footer'
    Frame: 'template-content' (this is content_for_layout zone)
      Frame: 'section-product-information'
        Component: 'block-product-image'
        Component: 'block-product-title-price'
        Component: 'block-variant-picker'
        Component: 'block-add-to-cart'
        Component: 'block-product-description'
      Frame: 'section-product-recommendations'
        Component: 'block-product-card' (repeated)

FIGMA IMPLICATION: In every new design page, set up the layout frame immediately. Add a Figma annotation (using Annotation feature or sticky note) on each section frame showing: 'Shopify file: sections/[name].liquid'. Add a 'Template' annotation on the page: 'Shopify template: templates/[name].json'. This lets developers skim your Figma file and know exactly what files to create without guessing.

title: Shopify Dev Handoff — Annotating Settings Schema for Developers
Shopify Dev Handoff — Variant Selector Annotation Guide
content:
Variant selectors require precise annotation because the implementation (swatch, pill, dropdown) affects JS complexity, accessibility requirements, and the dev scope. Never hand off a variant selector without full state and behaviour documentation.

SELECTOR TYPES & FEASIBILITY:
Dropdown (`<select>`): NATIVE. Standard HTML select. No JS for rendering (JS needed only for image/price update on change). Use when: many options (5+), mobile primary experience, simple theme.
Pill/Button: LIQUID. Custom rendering of `product.options_with_values`. JS required for selection state, unavailable state, price/image update. Use when: few options (2–6), options are short text (S/M/L/XL), desktop-first.
Color swatch: LIQUID. Requires colour mapping (option value to hex/image) via metafield lookup or hardcoded map. JS required. Accessibility-heavy. Use when: option is 'Color' or 'Colour' and merchant maintains a colour catalogue.
Image swatch: LIQUID/CUSTOM. Same as color swatch but uses a thumbnail image per option. Requires variant image assignment in Admin. More dev complexity than flat colour.

ANNOTATION FORMAT (add to selector component in Figma):
Variant Selector: [Option Name]
Type: [dropdown | pill | color-swatch | image-swatch]
Options source: product.options_with_values (Liquid)
Selected state: [describe visually]
Unavailable state: [describe visually]
OOS behaviour: [hide | grey out | show with strikethrough]
JS note: Updates product.featured_image and price on selection
Accessibility: arrow-key navigation, aria-label per option, focus ring

EXAMPLE — Color Swatch:
Variant Selector: Color
Type: color-swatch
Options source: product.options_with_values where option.name == 'Color'
Colour data source: @metafield custom.swatch_color (hex string) per variant, or hardcoded map
Selected state: 3px solid border, colour = --color-foreground, 2px white gap between swatch and border
Hover state: subtle scale (1.05) + border colour = --color-foreground-40
Unavailable state: 50% opacity + diagonal strikethrough line (CSS)
Disabled state: cursor:not-allowed, no hover effect
Accessibility: role='radio', aria-label='{color name}', aria-checked='true/false', keyboard: arrow keys to navigate, Enter to select
Min size: 36×36px swatch, 44×44px touch target with padding

EXAMPLE — Pill Selector (Size):
Variant Selector: Size
Type: pill
Selected state: background = --color-primary, text = --color-primary-text, font-weight: 600
Unselected state: border 1px --color-border, background transparent, text --color-foreground
Hover state: background = --color-primary-10 (10% opacity of primary)
Unavailable state: text-decoration: line-through, opacity: 0.4, cursor: not-allowed
Min size: 44×44px
Note: If >8 options, switch to dropdown (`<select>`) on mobile breakpoint

SELLING PLAN SELECTOR (subscriptions):
Type: radio group (NEVER pill buttons)
Reason: Buttons compete with the main CTA. Radio inputs are semantically correct for mutually exclusive selections.
Selected state: radio dot filled, label text bold, optional plan details revealed below
Group layout: vertical stack, never side-by-side
Contains: one-time purchase option + one subscription option per group
Annotate: selling_plan_group.name as group label, selling_plan.name as option label
Price display: percentage savings (Save 10%) not absolute values (Save $3.00) — prices break with multi-currency

FIGMA IMPLICATION: For every variant option on a product page, create all required state variants in Figma: Default, Hover, Selected, Unavailable, Disabled. Name them [SelectorType]/[OptionName]/[State]. Include a 'Colour mapping' table as a sticky note if using color swatches — list each colour name and its hex value. This table is what developers use to build the lookup map.

title: Shopify Dev Handoff — Metafield Annotation for Designers
content:
Metafields power all custom product data beyond Shopify's standard fields. Designers must document metafield namespaces, keys, and types precisely — developers cannot build the Liquid output without knowing these.

METAFIELD ANATOMY:
Every metafield has three parts: {namespace}.{key} : {type}
Namespace: logical grouping (e.g., 'custom', 'product', 'shipping', your-brand-name')
Key: specific field name (e.g., 'badge', 'care_instructions', 'fit_notes')
Type: data type (determines what Liquid filter to use and how to render)

ANNOTATION FORMAT:
@metafield {namespace}.{key} : {type} — {how to display}

METAFIELD TYPE REFERENCE:
single_line_text_field — Short string. Render directly: {{ product.metafields.custom.badge.value }}. Use for: badges ('New', 'Bestseller', 'Limited'), brief labels, short specs.
multi_line_text_field — Multiline plain text. Render with line breaks. Use for: care instructions, material details, short paragraphs.
rich_text_field — Shopify-flavoured HTML (limited tags). Render with `| metafield_tag`. Use for: formatted descriptions, bulleted lists, links within text.
number_integer — Integer. Render directly or format with math filters. Use for: ratings out of 5, item counts.
number_decimal — Float/decimal. Use for: percentages, dimensions with decimals.
boolean — true/false. Use in Liquid conditionals. Use for: 'is_limited_edition', 'is_eco_certified', 'is_pre_order'. Never render the word 'true' to the page — use it to show/hide a badge or label.
date — ISO date string. Render with `| date: '%B %d, %Y'`. Use for: launch dates, sale end dates, restock dates.
json — JSON object. Parse with `| parse_json`. Use for: product specifications table (key-value pairs), size guides, technical details.
file_reference — Uploaded file ID. Render with `| file_img_url` (images) or `| file_url` (PDFs). Use for: care symbols image, size guide PDF, product certificate.
product_reference — Product GID. Render as linked product card. Use for: complementary product, bundled item, replacement product.
collection_reference — Collection GID. Render as featured collection. Use for: 'Shop this look' collection, related category.
page_reference — Page GID. Links to a Shopify page. Use for: size guide page link, policy page link.
url — URL string. External link. Use for: external certifications, supplier pages, social proof links.
rating — Object with `value` and `scale_max`. Render as star display. Use for: aggregate review scores from imported data.
color — Hex string with `#`. Render as CSS color value. Use for: swatch override colour, accent colour per product.
dimension — Object with `value` and `unit`. Render with unit conversion filters. Use for: physical dimensions, weight.
volume — Same as dimension, for liquid capacity. Use for: product volume, fill amount.
weight — Object with value and unit. Use for: product weight display.

EXAMPLE ANNOTATIONS — Product Page:
@metafield custom.badge : single_line_text_field — render as pill badge above title. Empty state: hide badge entirely.
@metafield custom.short_description : multi_line_text_field — render as secondary subheading below title. Empty state: collapse.
@metafield custom.care_instructions : rich_text_field — render inside collapsible 'Care' tab. Empty state: hide tab.
@metafield custom.specs : json — render as 2-column table (Label | Value). Empty state: hide specs section.
@metafield custom.eco_certified : boolean — if true, show 'Certified Eco' icon badge. Empty state (false): no badge.
@metafield custom.size_guide : file_reference — render as image in size guide modal. Empty state: hide 'Size guide' link.
@metafield custom.fit_notes : single_line_text_field — render as italic text below size selector ('Runs small — size up'). Empty state: hide.
@metafield reviews.rating : rating — render as 4.8 ★ (324 reviews). Empty state: hide entire reviews summary row.

EMPTY STATE RULE: Every metafield annotation must include an empty state instruction. Developers wrap every metafield render in a conditional ({% if product.metafields.custom.badge != blank %}). Design the 'no metafield' state and annotate it explicitly — otherwise the section breaks for products that don't have the field populated.

SETTING UP IN SHOPIFY ADMIN: Developers create metafield definitions in Admin > Settings > Custom data > Metafields. Designers should provide a 'Metafield Definitions' spec (can be a Figma table or doc): columns are Namespace, Key, Type, Name (display label in admin), Validation (e.g., max characters), Required (yes/no). This prevents miscommunication about field names and types.

FIGMA IMPLICATION: Add a 'Metafield definitions' frame to every handoff file. It should be a table listing every metafield used in the design with: Namespace.Key | Type | Display pattern | Empty state. Pin this frame to the Figma cover page so developers find it immediately.

title: Shopify Dev Handoff — Token Naming & Responsive Breakpoints
content:
CSS custom property (token) naming and responsive breakpoints are the foundation of a Shopify theme's design system. Designers must annotate token usage and design at all three breakpoints.

TOKEN NAMING MODEL:
Shopify Horizon and modern Shopify themes use this pattern:
--{category}-{semantic}[-{modifier}]
Categories: color, font, spacing, border, shadow, animation, layer (z-index)

COLOR TOKENS:
--color-foreground — primary text colour (high contrast on background)
--color-foreground-40 — 40% opacity foreground (secondary text, icons)
--color-background — page background
--color-primary — primary action colour (buttons, links, accents)
--color-primary-text — text that appears ON the primary colour background
--color-secondary — secondary/muted action colour
--color-border — default border colour
--color-error — error state (form validation, out of stock warning)
--color-success — success state (added to cart, form submitted)
--color-scheme-* — scheme-scoped tokens that change per colour scheme (Horizon uses 6 schemes)

TYPOGRAPHY TOKENS:
--font-family-body — body text font
--font-family-heading — heading font (may differ from body)
--font-family-accent — accent/display font (optional)
--font-size-base — base body size (typically 16px)
--font-weight-bold — bold weight (600 or 700)
--line-height-body — body line-height (typically 1.5)
--line-height-tight — heading line-height (typically 1.1–1.2)

SPACING TOKENS (Horizon scale):
--spacing-3xs: 4px
--spacing-2xs: 8px
--spacing-xs: 12px
--spacing-sm: 16px
--spacing-md: 20px
--spacing-lg: 28px
--spacing-xl: 36px
--spacing-2xl: 44px
--spacing-3xl: 52px
Derived tokens: --page-margin (16px mobile / 40px desktop), --section-gap, --component-gap

BORDER TOKENS:
--border-width: 1px (default)
--border-radius-sm: 4px
--border-radius-md: 8px
--border-radius-lg: 16px
--border-radius-pill: 999px (for pills and tags)

ANIMATION TOKENS:
--duration-fast: 150ms
--duration-medium: 250ms
--duration-slow: 350ms
--easing-standard: cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)
--easing-decelerate: cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1) (elements entering screen)
--easing-accelerate: cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1) (elements leaving screen)

LAYER (Z-INDEX) TOKENS:
--layer-flat: 0
--layer-raised: 1 (cards, dropdowns)
--layer-sticky: 100 (sticky header/bar)
--layer-overlay: 200 (filter drawer, modal backdrop)
--layer-modal: 300 (modals, lightboxes)
--layer-toast: 400 (notification toasts)

RESPONSIVE BREAKPOINTS:
Shopify themes standardize on these media query breakpoints:
Mobile: <750px — Figma frame: 375px wide (or 430px for larger phones)
Tablet: 750px–989px — Figma frame: 750px wide
Desktop: ≥990px — Figma frame: 1200px wide (or 1440px for large desktop check)
Container max-width (content within page margins):
  Narrow: ~550px (text-focused pages)
  Normal: ~1200px (standard layouts)
  Wide: ~1400px (image-forward, full-bleed)
Page margin: 16px (mobile), 40px (tablet+)

COMMON RESPONSIVE LAYOUT PATTERNS:
1-column (mobile) → 2-column (tablet) → 3–4 column (desktop) for product grids
Full-width image (mobile) → 50/50 split (tablet+) for feature sections
Stacked nav (mobile hamburger) → horizontal nav (desktop) for header
Bottom drawer (mobile) → side panel (tablet+) for filter

FIGMA ANNOTATION PRACTICE:
For every styled element, annotate token name in Figma notes:
  Button primary background: @token color-primary
  Button primary text: @token color-primary-text
  Button border-radius: @token border-radius-md
  Button padding: @token spacing-sm (vertical) @token spacing-md (horizontal)
  Heading font: @token font-family-heading, @token line-height-tight
  Body text: @token font-family-body, @token font-size-base, @token line-height-body
  Card border: 1px solid @token color-border
  Card shadow: @token shadow-sm
  Transition: @token duration-fast @token easing-standard

FIGMA IMPLICATION: Create a Figma frame called 'Token Map' in your handoff file. It should list every token used across sections, with its CSS variable name, current value, and what elements use it. If you're designing with Figma variables, the variable name should match the CSS custom property name exactly — this makes developer translation trivial. For each artboard/page, design at all three breakpoints (375px, 750px, 1200px) as separate frames, clearly labelled 'Mobile', 'Tablet', 'Desktop'.

title: Shopify Dev Handoff — Edge Cases & Liquid Conditional States Designers Must Provide
content:
Shopify themes must handle missing, incomplete, or extreme data gracefully. Designers who only design the happy path create costly back-and-forth during development. Every design must address these edge cases.

PRODUCT AVAILABILITY STATES — Design all of these:
Available (default): Add to cart button active, full price shown, all variants selectable.
Sold out (product.available == false): Button text 'Sold out', button disabled, no add-to-cart form.
Variant unavailable (product.selected_variant.available == false): Specific variant greyed/struck through in selector; button shows 'Unavailable' or 'Notify me'.
Low stock (inventory_quantity <= 3): 'Only X left' badge near selector or button. Annotate the threshold number.
Pre-order (selling_plan with deferred payment): Button text changes to 'Pre-order', shipping estimate shown.

CONTENT EDGE CASES — Design explicit variants for:
No product image: Use a themed placeholder (icon + brand colour background, NOT a broken image icon).
Single product image: Hide thumbnail carousel navigation (dots/arrows become confusing with 1 image).
Many product images (10+): Show thumbnail strip with scroll indicator; cap visible thumbnails at 5–6, rest scroll.
Long product title (3+ lines): Text wraps; card height must expand or text truncates with ellipsis. Annotate which behaviour.
Short product title (1–2 words): Card should not look sparse — price/vendor fill the space correctly.
No product description: Collapse description tab or section. Never show empty tab.
Long product description: Collapsible 'Read more' at ~3 lines. Annotate the collapse height in px.
No sale price: `compare_at_price` absent — hide strikethrough price entirely.
No vendor: `product.vendor` empty — hide vendor name, no gap left.
No metafield: Hide the block. Never show a blank label with no value.
No reviews: Hide star rating row and 'Write a review' tab.

COLLECTION & SEARCH STATES:
Empty collection (0 products): 'No products' friendly message + optional call to action (Browse all).
Filtered to zero products: 'No products match your filters' + 'Clear all filters' button. Design this state explicitly.
Search: no results: 'No results for [query]' + suggested searches or popular products.
Search: one result: Grid shows single product without looking orphaned.
Collection with 1 product: Grid shows single product; pagination hidden.

FORM & INTERACTIVE STATES:
Form default: All fields empty, labels visible.
Form focus: Active field has visible focus ring (2px, colour = --color-primary).
Form error: Red border + error message below field. Never colour alone — include text.
Form success: Green confirmation or page redirect. Design the success state.
Cart empty: Empty cart message + CTA to continue shopping. Not a blank page.
Cart with many items: Scroll behaviour in drawer; sticky 'Checkout' button at bottom.

LIQUID CONDITIONAL QUICK REFERENCE FOR ANNOTATIONS:
Annotate conditionals in Figma notes using this format:
@if product.available → [design for this state]
@if product.available == false → [sold out design]
@if product.on_sale → [show strikethrough + sale price]
@if product.selected_variant.available == false → [unavailable variant state]
@if product.metafields.custom.badge != blank → [show badge]
@if product.metafields.custom.badge == blank → [hide badge — no gap]
@if collection.all_products_count == 0 → [empty collection design]
@if search.results_count == 0 → [no search results design]
@if product.description != blank → [show description tab]
@if product.description == blank → [hide description tab]
@if product.images.size > 1 → [show thumbnail carousel]
@if product.images.size == 1 → [hide carousel navigation]
@if cart.item_count > 0 → [normal cart]
@if cart.item_count == 0 → [empty cart state]

COMPONENT VARIANT NAMING IN FIGMA:
For every component that has edge case states, create explicit Figma component variants:
ProductCard/Available — default happy path
ProductCard/SoldOut — `product.available == false`
ProductCard/LowStock — inventory_quantity <= 3
ProductCard/OnSale — `product.on_sale`
ProductCard/NoImage — `product.featured_image == nil`
ProductCard/LongTitle — 3+ line title

FIGMA IMPLICATION: Every component in the design system must have a complete variant set covering the states above. Mark edge case variants as 'Not for client presentation — for developer reference' in the Figma description. Organize them in a 'States & Edge Cases' section on the component page. Developers build these states in Liquid conditionals — without the design reference, they'll either skip them or improvise inconsistently.

title: Shopify Dev Handoff — App Block Slots, Constraints & Handoff Checklist
content:
App blocks are how Shopify apps inject UI into themes. Designers must annotate where app blocks can go and what constraints apply — otherwise developers must guess, and apps may break the layout.

APP BLOCK ARCHITECTURE:
App blocks appear as special block types in a section's schema. The theme specifies which sections accept app blocks by including `"type": "@app"` in the blocks list. Merchants add app blocks via Theme Editor by dragging them into sections that accept them. The app provides the block's HTML/CSS/JS — the theme only provides the slot.

WHERE APP BLOCKS GO — ANNOTATE EACH SLOT:
Product page: Most common location. Typical apps: Reviews (Yotpo, Judge.me), size recommenders, loyalty points, custom tabs, live chat. Annotate: '@app-block product-page: accepts 1–3 blocks, no fixed height'
Cart page/drawer: Upsell apps, gift message, giftwrap options. Annotate: '@app-block cart: 1 app block max, avoid below checkout button'
Collection page: Filter apps, sort apps, search apps (if replacing native). Rare — native filtering preferred. Annotate: '@app-block collection: only if replacing native filter'
Home page: Popups, announcement banners, chat widgets, social proof feeds. Annotate: '@app-block homepage: accept multiple, design for stacking'
Header: Rare — usually chat bubbles or cookie banners. Annotate: '@app-block header: floating/overlay apps only'
Order confirmation: Post-purchase upsells (Shopify Plus / checkout extensions only). Annotate: '@app-block post-purchase: Shopify Plus required'

APP BLOCK DESIGN CONSTRAINTS:
— App blocks have no guaranteed dimensions. Design the slot with flexible height.
— Multiple app blocks may stack vertically. Design the section to handle 2–3 stacked blocks.
— App block may fail to load (app uninstalled, network error). Design the section to look correct without it.
— App blocks are merchant-controlled — merchants can add/remove them in Theme Editor. Never assume an app block will always be present.
— App blocks cannot nest inside other app blocks.
— App blocks do not inherit the parent section's colour scheme by default — they use their own app styling. Annotate this: 'App block styling is app-controlled; cannot be guaranteed to match design system tokens.'

DESIGN PATTERNS FOR APP BLOCK SLOTS:
1. Reserve space — Design a placeholder in the layout where the app block will go. Label it with '[App Block: Reviews]' or '[App Block: Size Guide]' as a Figma annotation, not as visual UI.
2. Flexible containers — The container holding the app block should be `height: auto` and `width: 100%` — never fixed dimensions.
3. No visual dependency — The section above and below the app block slot must look correct if the app block is absent.
4. Annotate Z-index — App blocks that float (chat widgets, badges) need a z-index annotation: use `--layer-raised` (not hardcoded numbers).

DEV HANDOFF CHECKLIST — FINAL REVIEW:
Before marking a handoff as ready, verify:
[ ] Every template page (product, collection, cart, home, etc.) has a separate Figma page named 'template-[name]'
[ ] Every section frame is named 'section-[name]' and maps to a Shopify section file
[ ] Every block component is named 'block-[name]' and has a @setting annotation for each configurable element
[ ] All variant selectors have: type, all states (default/hover/selected/unavailable/disabled), accessibility notes, and JS behaviour note
[ ] All metafields are listed in a 'Metafield Definitions' table with namespace, key, type, and empty state
[ ] Token map is documented: CSS variable name → current value → what uses it
[ ] Three responsive frames exist per template: 375px (mobile), 750px (tablet), 1200px (desktop)
[ ] All liquid conditional states are annotated (@if conditions) on components that depend on data
[ ] All app block slots are identified and labelled with the expected app type
[ ] Edge case variants exist for: no image, sold out, low stock, empty collection, no reviews, long title, no description
[ ] Feasibility annotations are on every section/component: Native | Liquid | Custom(App)
[ ] Touch targets are 44×44px minimum for all interactive elements
[ ] Colour contrast passes: 4.5:1 body text, 3:1 large text (>18px or bold >14px)
[ ] Focus states are visible on all interactive elements (buttons, links, inputs, selectors, swatches)
[ ] Every price is marked as dynamic (never hardcoded in Figma text — use placeholder {{ product.price | money }})
[ ] Checkout-customization elements are flagged as 'Shopify Plus required' if they modify checkout layout
[ ] All section/block designs work independently (no section depends on adjacent sections for visual coherence)

FIGMA IMPLICATION: Create a 'Handoff Index' frame as the first frame in every design file. It should contain: (1) a feasibility legend (green=Native, amber=Liquid, red=Custom/App), (2) a metafield definitions table, (3) a token map summary, (4) a list of every app block slot with the expected app, (5) a checklist confirming all states and edge cases have been designed. This frame is for developers — pin it so it is always visible when the file opens.
